name: @jipika/dsh-memory
description: Progressive long-term memory for DSH: sharded markdown bodies under ~/.dsh/memory/topics/, with only a live-generated map (shard · keywords · count · latest date) injected into the system prompt, entries pulled on demand via grep + read — so the prompt cost stays flat however large the memory grows. Two layers (global + per-project) plus the global rule files, viewable AND editable in DSH Settings, with per-layer switches and an index/full injection toggle. v0.5.0 adds enforcement hooks: a write guard on the native tool pipeline (format/secrets/history rules, optional external command judge, deny/ask with reasons fed back to the model), post-write audit log, a read reminder when memory files are read, a mandatory discipline block, and an optional injection filter command. Zero extra LLM cost, live re-read. v0.5.1 keeps the switches in ~/.dsh/memory/settings.json — read live by the plugin and edited from the settings pane over the plugin's own route, independent of the host settings API. v0.6.0 fixes the index silently degrading to a title-less directory once memory outgrew the hardcoded 9k budget (which is why an agent could see memory injected and still never read it): the index now shrinks per-shard along a newest-N-per-shard ladder under a configurable indexBudget, adds per-shard keywords (routing hint) and latest-entry dates, ships a 'check memory before starting a task' discipline, and makes full mode read the shard bodies (auto-falling back to index when over budget) instead of the retired memory.md navigation file. v0.7.0 makes 'map' the default injection mode (shard-level map only, no entry titles): retrieval = grep the memory dir with task keywords, then read the matched line; layers with <=12 entries stay inlined; the discipline block teaches that two-step path and routes cross-shard lookups (>=3 entries / >=2 shards / >=3k body) to a subagent that returns facts + line numbers instead of raw bodies. v0.9.0 adds the card-memory layer for roleplay sessions and makes every path Windows-safe: home resolution follows os.homedir() (so an undefined or empty HOME no longer roots paths at the drive root), tool and bash paths are normalized before guard matching, and drive-letter cwds produce valid project slugs. v0.9.2 fixes retrieval ranking at scale (IDF-weighted entry scores, df=0 CJK bigram fragments excluded from the coverage gate, BM25-style length normalization, preview windows anchored on the rarest matched token instead of a fixed 240-char head cut; measured locally: shards covered per top-8 2.88->5.75, largest tie block 4.38->1.13, previews containing a matched token 67%->100%): shard-level bonuses no longer inflate every entry in that shard (they were added inside the entry loop, so all hits from one shard shared an identical score and ordering collapsed to date-then-line), a per-shard quota stops one shard from filling the whole result page, and the default scope is the current project layer (other projects' shards — 60% of the pool locally — are skipped but reported in dropped.offScopeLayers/offScopeFiles, with scope:'all' to opt back in).
